content.text: `alinea/nuxt` adds Alinea to a Nuxt app with a single module. It serves the dashboard and the Alinea API from your Nuxt server, lets your server routes query drafts while an editor previews a page, and refreshes the page data on every edit without reloading.
Install
Install Alinea next to Nuxt. The dashboard is built with React, so add `react` and `react-dom` as well:
Create the CMS

Create your CMS with `createCMS` from `alinea/server` in `cms.ts` in the root of your project, or in `src/cms.ts`. The Alinea CLI and the Nuxt module look for it there. `baseUrl` is where your site runs, `handlerUrl` the route of the Alinea API and `adminPath` the path of the dashboard:
Add the module
Add `alinea/nuxt` to the modules in your Nuxt config:
The module picks up the `cms` exported from `cms.ts` and adds a server plugin that, for every request:
proxies the dashboard to the Alinea CLI during development,
answers the handler route, `GET` requests for media files under `/admin/file/` and the dashboard route `/admin` itself,
otherwise runs the request with its draft state, so queries see drafts when an editor previews the page.
There are no server files to write for Alinea itself.
Query content

`cms.ts` runs on the server only: it reads the generated content database and signs requests with your API key. Query it in server routes, and load their results in your pages with `useFetch`, which runs on the server while rendering and in the browser when navigating. Never import `cms` into a Vue component. A route that answers the page at a url:
And a catch-all page that renders it:
`useFetch` infers the type of `page` from the route. During server rendering Nuxt calls the route directly and passes along the cookies of the request, so drafts show up there too.
Develop and build
Run Nuxt through the Alinea CLI. It generates your content database, starts the dashboard and passes its location to Nuxt in environment variables:

Open `http://localhost:3000/admin` to edit content. `alinea build` writes the production dashboard into your `public` folder and generates the content database, then runs the Nuxt build. In production `/admin` redirects to the dashboard at `/admin.html`.
Live previews

The dashboard previews an entry by loading its page with a preview token. The handler turns that into a signed draft cookie and redirects to the page. The module then adds a small script to draft pages, which receives the edits from the dashboard. On every edit it calls `refreshNuxtData()`, so `useFetch` and `useAsyncData` load the new content without reloading the page or losing its state. This keeps working after navigating to other pages.
Show the floating preview toolbar with the `widget` option, or set `previews: false` to leave draft pages untouched:
Handler options
To configure the handler, for example with a
custom backend
or commit hooks, add the plugin yourself with `createNitroPlugin`. It takes the same options as `createMiddleware` from `alinea/server` and replaces the plugin the module adds:
Deploy

Deploy to a Node runtime, such as the default `node-server` preset: pages query the SQLite database generated in `@alinea/generated`. Nitro traces it into `.output/server/node_modules`, so `node .output/server/index.mjs` runs without the rest of your `node_modules`.
Set `ALINEA_API_KEY` in the production environment. The handler uses it to sign preview tokens and draft cookies, and to talk to its backend.
The handler saves edits as commits through
Alinea Cloud or your own backend
. Running servers sync their database with the handler at `baseUrl`, so published changes show without a redeploy.
Static generation

`alinea build -- nuxt generate` prerenders your pages from the generated database: Nuxt calls your server routes while prerendering and stores their results in the payload of each page, so navigating needs no server. A static site has no handler though, so the dashboard cannot save and there are no live previews. Edit content with `alinea dev` locally and deploy the result, or deploy to a Node server to edit in production.
